topic: Seasons are not caused by distance
claim: Earth's 23.4-degree axial tilt, not its distance from the Sun, causes the seasons; Earth is closest to the Sun in January.

beats.caption: Closest in January
beats.vo: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere. It's farthest away in July.

beats.caption: The real cause: a 23.4° tilt
beats.vo: The real cause is tilt. Earth's axis leans 23.4 degrees. The half of Earth tilted toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight, and that's its summer.

beats.caption: Tilt wins
beats.vo: The distance changes by only about 3 million miles out of 93 million. Too small to matter. Tilt wins. So right now, which half of Earth is leaning toward the Sun?

sources.text: NASA Science, Earth Facts: axis tilted 23.4 degrees, which causes the seasons; average distance 93 million miles. https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/
NASA Space Place, What Causes the Seasons?: perihelion ~91.4 million miles (January), aphelion ~94.5 million miles (July). https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/seasons/en/
